title: Temporal Feature Engineering and Threshold Optimization for Early Warning in Healthcare Claims Anomaly Detection
tldr: Develops a comprehensive framework for temporal feature engineering and adaptive threshold optimization for early warning in healthcare claims anomaly detection, achieving 87% detection rate with 6% false positive rate on Medicare Part B claims data.
problem_and_motivation: Healthcare expenditure in the US exceeds $4.3 trillion annually, with fraud rates ranging from 3-10% ($129-430 billion in potential losses). Existing approaches rely on manually engineered features limiting discovery of novel fraud patterns, while threshold selection challenges include balancing detection sensitivity with operational constraints and managing false positive rates.
approach: Developed a systematic temporal feature engineering framework combining statistical analysis, machine learning-based feature construction, and deep learning representations.
Extracted 127 distinct temporal features from Medicare Part B claims data (2020-2022) including service interval patterns, claim frequency characteristics, and seasonal variation indicators.
Implemented LSTM autoencoder embeddings to learn compact temporal representations of claims sequences.
Proposed adaptive threshold optimization methodology that adjusts detection thresholds based on historical false positive rates and investigative capacity constraints.
Conducted comprehensive evaluation using stratified five-fold cross-validation on 47.3 million claims from 892,450 healthcare providers.
findings: Detection rates improved from 0.73 for baseline features to 0.87 for the complete temporal feature set.
False positive rates decreased from 0.14 to 0.06 while maintaining operational feasibility.
Area under the ROC curve increased from 0.84 to 0.93, indicating significantly improved discrimination.
Service-to-submission lag standard deviation ranked highest in feature importance with score of 0.089.
LSTM autoencoder embeddings provided 0.06 improvement over statistical features alone.
Net annual savings of $156 million for Medicare program operations with the optimized approach.
Adaptive framework maintained stable detection rates within 0.03 range despite concept drift events.

Figure 2: LSTM Autoencoder Embedding Space Visualization → Displays t-SNE projections of 128-dimensional embeddings showing natural separation of legitimate and fraudulent providers.
Figure 3: Threshold Performance Trade-off Curves → Multi-curve graph showing detection rate, false positive rate, investigation volume, and cost savings as functions of threshold values.
Table 1: Temporal Interval Feature Taxonomy → Comprehensive taxonomy of temporal interval features including service-to-submission lag, inter-service intervals, and beneficiary patterns.
Table 4: Deep Learning Feature Construction Performance → Comparison of LSTM autoencoder, LSTM with attention, bidirectional LSTM, and graph neural network architectures.
Table 7: Cost-Benefit Analysis for Threshold Selection → Shows detection rates, false positive rates, and net benefits for different threshold values.

definitions.definition: Process of extracting meaningful temporal features from claims sequential data including service interval patterns, claim frequency characteristics, and seasonal variation indicators.
Deep learning architecture that learns compact representations of temporal claims sequences through encoder-decoder networks, where reconstruction error serves as an anomaly indicator.
Methodology that dynamically adjusts detection thresholds based on historical false positive rates and operational constraints to balance detection sensitivity with investigation capacity.
Occurs when statistical properties of fraud patterns change over time, requiring threshold recalibration to maintain detection effectiveness.
Functional Principal Component Analysis providing dimensionality reduction for temporal trajectories while preserving essential dynamic characteristics.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a comprehensive framework for temporal feature engineering and adaptive threshold optimization for early warning in healthcare claims anomaly detection. The key innovation is the systematic extraction of 127 temporal features combined with LSTM autoencoder embeddings, achieving 87% detection rate with 6% false positive rate. The adaptive threshold mechanism maintains stable performance despite concept drift, while the cost-benefit analysis demonstrates $156 million annual savings potential. The framework processes 15,000 providers per hour with 2.4-second latency, enabling practical deployment.
directly_justifies: Detection rates improved from 0.73 to 0.87 through temporal feature engineering.
False positive rates decreased from 0.14 to 0.06 while maintaining operational feasibility.
Area under ROC curve increased from 0.84 to 0.93 indicating significantly improved discrimination.
Service-to-submission lag standard deviation ranked highest in feature importance with 0.089 score.
Net annual savings of $156 million for Medicare program operations.
limits: Evaluation relies exclusively on Medicare Part B claims data, which may not generalize to other healthcare systems.
Fraud prevalence of 0.43% poses challenges for model calibration in low-prevalence settings.
Computational requirements for deep learning feature construction may limit accessibility for smaller organizations.
Threshold optimization assumes stable cost parameters while actual costs exhibit uncertainty and temporal variation.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domains 8.A and 8.B received high relevance as the paper's core contribution is anomaly detection for fraud. Domain 6.A received high relevance for predictive modeling implementation. Domain 6.B received medium relevance for sequential pattern analysis. Domain 12.A received high relevance for comprehensive evaluation methodology. Other domains were considered but rejected as the paper focuses on healthcare claims rather than personal finance, budgeting, or expense categorization.

limitations: Evaluation relies exclusively on Medicare Part B claims data with fee-for-service reimbursement structures.
Class imbalance with 0.43% fraud prevalence poses challenges for model calibration and performance estimation.
Computational requirements for deep learning feature construction may limit accessibility for smaller healthcare organizations.
Threshold optimization assumes stable cost parameters while actual costs exhibit uncertainty and temporal variation.
